value.rationale: The same canonical random circumscription provides two geometrically natural approximation errors. A complete sharp conditional area spectrum at fixed maximal radial error, with an actual nonattainment transition, is a meaningful finite-size geometric constraint. The joint product theorem distinguishes bulk and extreme errors and their different normalizations, information relevant to simultaneously controlling average and worst-direction approximation. Already-known expected-area and generic spacing-CLT components are not passed off as contributions.
